questions.q: What is the correct general order of a Receivables period close?
options: Close the period, then finish month-end activity, then reconcile
Finish month-end activity, run final accounting, set Close Pending, reconcile, resolve differences, then close
Reconcile first, then enter all transactions for the period
Set Close Pending before any transactions are entered for the period
questions.explain: The close sequence finishes month-end activity, finalizes accounting, moves to Close Pending, reconciles against GL, resolves any differences, and only then closes fully.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Close Pending status?
options: It permanently locks the period immediately
It automatically writes off all open balances
It only applies to miscellaneous receipts
It is a transitional status that signals close is underway while still allowing corrections if reconciliation finds a problem
questions.explain: Close Pending is a middle state — it discourages further changes but still allows investigation and correction before the period is hard-closed.

questions.q: What does the Prepare Receivables to General Ledger Reconciliation process produce?
options: A customer statement for every open account
A dunning letter escalation schedule
A list of all approved write-offs for the year
A report comparing the Receivables-side balance to the GL-side balance by account
questions.explain: This process prepares data for the Receivables to Ledger Reconciliation Report, which lays the Receivables and GL balances side by side by account.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Differences report?
options: To automatically correct any reconciliation mismatch without review
To help pinpoint the specific cause of a difference found during reconciliation
To generate a new aging report
To replace the need for Create Accounting
questions.explain: The Differences report helps identify exactly why Receivables and GL don't match, such as an unaccounted transaction or a skipped transfer.

questions.q: Which of these would most likely explain a reconciliation difference?
options: A customer statement was printed for a current account
A collector sent a friendly first dunning letter
A standard receipt was applied to the correct invoice
A transaction was accounted but never actually transferred and posted to GL
questions.explain: A transaction that was finalized in Receivables but never transferred and posted to GL is a classic cause of a reconciliation difference.
